# `scikitplot.visualkeras`

<!-- Generated by `python tools/maint_tools/generate_usage_skills.py sync` from the installed package; edit the module's docstrings or `__all__`, not this file. -->

## Install

```sh
pip install scikit-plots
```

The release on PyPI can be older than the version this skill was read from, and
can lack `scikitplot.visualkeras`. If `import scikitplot.visualkeras` fails
after installing it, the installed release predates the module: the [release
history on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/scikit-plots/#history) lists each
release, and [pip's user guide](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/user_guide/)
explains upgrading.

## Read the API of the installed version

The table below was read from one version of scikit-plots; the project may
have another, and the installed package decides. Check the version, then read
what it declares (shown for `SpacingDummyLayer`; use the name you need):

```sh
python -c "import scikitplot; print(scikitplot.__version__)"
python -m scikitplot api scikitplot.visualkeras
python -c "import scikitplot.visualkeras as m; print(m.__all__)"
python -c "import scikitplot.visualkeras as m; help(m.SpacingDummyLayer)"
python -c "import inspect, scikitplot.visualkeras as m; print(inspect.signature(m.SpacingDummyLayer))"
```

- `python -m scikitplot api` lists every public name with its kind, signature
  and summary (`--name NAME` for one in full, `--format json` for tools).
  Releases before it report an error instead (an unknown command, or a
  missing dependency of an older command line): then use the next lines,
  which work on every release.
- `__all__` is the public list; `help()` is the full documentation of one name,
  methods included; `inspect.signature` is its exact call signature.
- Both read the installed objects. If they ever differ, `help()` and
  `inspect.signature` are the source of truth.

## Public API

Declared in `scikitplot.visualkeras.__all__`, in that order.

| Name | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `SpacingDummyLayer` | class | A factory class for dynamically generating a dummy Keras layer with custom spacing. |
| `graph_view` | function | Generates an architectural visualization for a given linear Keras `Model` model (i.e., one input and output tensor for each layer) in graph style. |
| `layered_view` | function | Generates an architectural visualization for a given linear Keras `Model` model (i.e., one input and output tensor for each layer) in a layered style, which is particularly suitable for convolutional neural networks (CNNs). |

All names with their signatures, from the installed version: `python -m scikitplot api scikitplot.visualkeras`
(or `print(m.__all__)` and `help()`, above).
